description: State Machine Builder page -- design and manage state machine configs with states, transitions, graph visualization, pathfinding, discovery exploration, live testing, and import/export. Users select or create configs from a header dropdown, then work across seven tabs: Graph (visual node-edge layout via dagre), States (table view), Transitions (list view), Pathfinding (find optimal paths between states), Discovery (automated state exploration with strategies), Live Test (manual transition execution and navigation), and Export/Import (JSON file operations).

groups.name: Page Header and Config Selector
groups.description: The page header shows a GitBranch icon, the title 'State Machine', and a config selector dropdown. Users pick an existing config to load it, or click 'New' to create one. A trash icon deletes the active config with a confirmation dialog. A loading spinner appears during async operations.

assertions.description: The page displays a clear 'State Machine' title in the header so users know they are on the state machine builder
Users see a config selector dropdown with a 'Select config...' placeholder option to choose which state machine config to work with
Users can click the 'New' button to begin creating a new state machine config
When a config is active, a trash icon button allows users to delete it after confirmation
preconditions: An active config must be selected

groups.name: Empty State (No Config Selected)
groups.description: When no config is selected, the page shows a centered empty state with a GitBranch icon and instructional text prompting the user to select or create a config.

assertions.description: When no config is selected, users see instructional text guiding them to select or create a config

criteria.textContent: Select a config or create a new one to get started.

assertions.description: Even in the empty state, the config selector dropdown is present so users can select an existing config
When no config is selected, the tab bar should not be visible since there is no config data to work with

target.label: Tab bar absent in empty state

groups.name: Create Config Flow
groups.description: Clicking 'New' reveals an inline input with a text field for the config name, a 'Create' button, and a 'Cancel' button. Users type a name and press Enter or click Create to persist the config via the sm_create_config IPC command.

assertions.description: The new config input field shows a 'Config name...' placeholder to indicate what to type
A 'Create' button submits the new config name to the backend
A 'Cancel' button dismisses the new config input without creating anything
The Create button is disabled when the name input is empty, preventing submission of blank config names
assertions.expected: The Create button should be visually disabled (opacity-50) when the name field is empty or whitespace-only

groups.name: Tab Navigation Bar
groups.description: Seven tabs appear below the header when a config is active: Graph, States, Transitions, Pathfinding, Discovery, Live Test, and Export / Import. The active tab is highlighted with a brand-primary bottom border. Each tab has an icon and label.

assertions.description: The Graph tab provides access to the interactive dagre-based node-edge visualization of states and transitions
The States tab shows a tabular view of all states in the config with selection support
The Transitions tab lists all transitions between states with selection and editing support
The Pathfinding tab enables users to find optimal paths between states in the config graph
The Discovery tab provides automated state exploration with configurable strategies
The Live Test tab provides manual controls to execute transitions and navigate to states
The Export / Import tab provides JSON file export and import operations for state machine configs
Exactly 7 tabs are rendered in the tab bar when a config is active
assertions.expected: The tab bar section below the header should contain exactly 7 tab buttons: Graph, States, Transitions, Pathfinding, Discovery, Live Test, Export / Import

groups.name: Graph Tab Content
groups.description: The Graph tab renders an interactive node-edge graph using @xyflow/react with dagre layout. States are nodes and transitions are edges. Floating action buttons allow adding new states and transitions. Clicking a node selects that state; clicking an edge selects the transition. An empty graph shows an instructional message.

assertions.description: A floating 'Add State' button on the graph tab allows users to create a new state, opening the new-state form in the sidebar
A floating 'Add Transition' button on the graph tab allows users to create a new transition between states
When no states exist, the graph shows an instructional empty message guiding users to import or use Discovery
preconditions: A config is selected with zero states

assertions.description: Clicking a state node in the graph selects it and opens the state detail sidebar, deselecting any previously selected transition
assertions.expected: Clicking a state node should: (1) highlight the node, (2) open the right sidebar showing 'State Detail' header, (3) deselect any previously selected transition
preconditions: A config is selected with at least one state

groups.name: States Tab Content
groups.description: The States tab shows a tabular/list view of all states using the shared StateViewPanel component. It has an 'Add State' button in the top-right corner. Clicking a state row selects it and opens the sidebar.

assertions.description: The States tab has its own 'Add State' button in the top-right corner for creating new states while viewing the state list

target.label: Add State button on states tab

assertions.description: Clicking a state in the states tab selects it and opens the state detail sidebar for editing
assertions.expected: Clicking a state row should select the state, open the right sidebar with 'State Detail' header, and allow editing the state's properties
preconditions: A config is selected with at least one state

groups.name: Transitions Tab Content
groups.description: The Transitions tab shows a list of all transitions using the shared TransitionsPanel component. It has an 'Add Transition' button in the top-right corner. Clicking a transition selects it and opens the sidebar.

assertions.description: The Transitions tab has its own 'Add Transition' button in the top-right corner for creating new transitions

target.label: Add Transition button on transitions tab

assertions.description: Clicking a transition in the list selects it and opens the transition editor sidebar
assertions.expected: Clicking a transition row should select the transition, open the right sidebar with 'Transition Detail' header, and allow editing the transition's properties
preconditions: A config is selected with at least one transition

groups.name: Sidebar: New State Form
groups.description: When 'Add State' is clicked, a right sidebar (w-80) opens with a 'New State' header, a Name input, a Description textarea, and a 'Create State' submit button. The sidebar has a close (X) button. The name field has placeholder 'e.g., Login Page' and description has 'Optional description'. Enter key in the name field submits if non-empty. The button is disabled when the name is empty or creation is in progress.

assertions.description: The sidebar shows a 'NEW STATE' header label so users know they are creating a new state
Users see a Name input field with placeholder 'e.g., Login Page' for entering the new state's name
Users see a Description textarea with placeholder 'Optional description' for entering a description of the state
A 'Create State' button submits the new state to the backend via the sm_create_state IPC command
The sidebar has a close button (X icon) with aria-label 'Close sidebar' to dismiss the sidebar panel
A 'Name' label identifies the state name input field

groups.name: Sidebar: State Detail Panel
groups.description: When a state is selected (by clicking a graph node or state row), the sidebar shows a 'State Detail' header and renders the shared StateDetailPanel component with fields for editing the state's properties, plus save and delete actions.

assertions.description: The sidebar shows a 'STATE DETAIL' header label when an existing state is selected for editing
The StateDetailPanel provides save and delete capabilities for the selected state, persisting changes via sm_update_state and sm_delete_state IPC commands
assertions.expected: The state detail panel should provide controls to edit and save the state's name, description, and other properties, as well as a delete button to remove the state
preconditions: Sidebar is open with State Detail header

groups.name: Sidebar: Transition Editor
groups.description: When a transition is selected, the sidebar shows a 'Transition Detail' header and renders the shared TransitionEditor component. When 'Add Transition' is clicked, the same TransitionEditor appears in create mode with a 'New Transition' header. The editor provides fields for from-states, to-states, name, actions, and path cost.

assertions.description: The sidebar shows a 'NEW TRANSITION' header label when creating a new transition
The sidebar shows a 'TRANSITION DETAIL' header label when an existing transition is selected
The TransitionEditor provides controls for editing transition properties including from-states, activate-states, name, actions list, and path cost
assertions.expected: The transition editor should show fields for editing from-states, activate-states, transition name, actions, and path cost, with save and delete capabilities
preconditions: A transition is selected or 'Add Transition' was clicked

groups.name: Export / Import Tab
groups.description: The Export/Import tab provides buttons to export the current config to a JSON file and import a config from a JSON file. It shows the current config summary (name, state count, transition count). Import errors are displayed in a red error banner. Export uses Tauri's save dialog; import uses Tauri's open dialog.

assertions.description: The export tab shows an 'Export / Import' section heading
An 'Export Config' button saves the active config as a JSON file through Tauri's save dialog
An 'Import Config' button opens Tauri's file picker to select a JSON config file for import
The export tab displays a summary of the current config showing its name and counts of states and transitions
The config summary shows the number of states and transitions (e.g., '5 states, 8 transitions')

groups.name: Discovery Tab: State Explorer Configure
groups.description: The Discovery tab is a multi-view panel (configure, history, report) for automated state exploration. In the configure view, users select an exploration strategy (smoke_test, exhaustive, regression, random_walk, targeted), configure advanced options (max states, state delay, screenshots, stop on failure), preview the exploration plan, and start an exploration run. The panel shows the config name and state/transition counts.

assertions.description: The discovery panel shows a 'State Explorer' heading in the configure view
A 'Strategy' label identifies the exploration strategy selector
Users can select an exploration strategy from a dropdown with options including Smoke Test, Exhaustive, Regression, Random Walk, and Targeted

target.label: Strategy selector with Smoke Test option

assertions.description: A 'Preview Plan' button generates and shows a preview of the exploration plan without running it
A 'Start Exploration' button begins the automated exploration run against the active config
An 'Advanced Options' toggle expands additional configuration fields for max states, state delay, screenshots, and stop-on-failure
A 'History' button navigates to the exploration history view showing past runs

groups.name: Discovery Tab: Advanced Options
groups.description: When the 'Advanced Options' toggle is expanded, it reveals configuration fields: Max states (number input, 0 = unlimited), State delay in ms (number input, default 500), Capture screenshots (checkbox, default on), Stop on first failure (checkbox, default off). These are shown in a left-bordered section.

assertions.description: A 'Max states (0 = unlimited)' label identifies the maximum states input
A 'State delay (ms)' label identifies the delay between state exploration steps
A 'Capture screenshots' checkbox allows toggling screenshot capture during exploration
A 'Stop on first failure' checkbox allows halting exploration when a failure is encountered

groups.name: Discovery Tab: Exploration History
groups.description: The history view shows a list of past exploration runs with config name, strategy, start timestamp, and summary. Each run has a 'View Report' link. A refresh button reloads the history, and a 'Clear runs older than 30 days' button purges old entries. When no runs exist, an empty state message is shown.

assertions.description: The history view shows an 'Exploration History' heading
When no exploration runs exist, the history shows 'No exploration runs yet' as an empty state
A 'Configure' back button returns to the configure view from the history view
A 'Clear runs older than 30 days' button purges stale exploration history entries
preconditions: History view with at least one run

groups.name: Discovery Tab: Exploration Report
groups.description: The report view shows detailed results of a single exploration run: summary stats (states passed/visited, transitions passed/verified, duration, strategy), per-state results with status icons, per-transition results with from/to labels, and an optional summary text. A 'Back' button returns to the history view.

assertions.description: The report view shows an 'Exploration Report' heading
The report shows a 'States Passed' stat card with the count of passed vs visited states
The report shows a 'Transitions Passed' stat card with the count of passed vs verified transitions
The report shows a 'Duration' stat card with the total exploration time
A 'Back' button returns from the report view to the history view

groups.name: Live Test Tab: Main Controls
groups.description: The Live Test tab provides interactive state machine testing. It has three sections: Execute Transition (with a searchable transition list and quick-execute buttons), Navigate to State (dropdown + navigate button), and an Activity Log. The tab requires a running Python executor.

assertions.description: The Live Test panel shows a 'Live Test' heading
A note reminds users that the Live Test requires a running executor process
An 'Execute Transition' section label identifies the transition execution area
Users can filter the transition list with a 'Filter transitions...' search input
A 'Navigate to State' section label identifies the state navigation area
A 'Navigate' button triggers navigation to the selected state via the navigate_to_state IPC command

groups.name: Live Test: Activity Log
groups.description: The activity log shows timestamped entries for transitions executed, navigations performed, info messages, and errors. Each entry is color-coded by type (blue for transitions, cyan for navigate, gray for info, red for errors). Refresh and clear buttons are provided. When empty, a placeholder message is shown.

assertions.description: An 'Activity Log' section label identifies the log area
When no activity has occurred, the log shows an instructional empty state message
A state selector dropdown with 'Select a state...' placeholder allows choosing a target state for navigation
When no transitions exist, the transition list shows 'No transitions' as an empty state
assertions.expected: When the config has no transitions, the transition list area should display 'No transitions' as placeholder text
preconditions: A config is selected with zero transitions

groups.name: Error Display and Loading States
groups.description: The page displays errors from the useStateMachineConfig hook in a red banner at the bottom of the page. Import errors appear in the export tab. The Live Test panel has its own error banner. Loading states are indicated by Loader2 spinner icons throughout the page.

assertions.description: When the useStateMachineConfig hook encounters an error, a red error banner appears at the bottom of the page displaying the error message
assertions.expected: When an IPC command fails (e.g., sm_list_configs, sm_create_config), a red-tinted banner should appear at the bottom of the page with the error message text. The banner has bg-red-500/10 background and red-500/20 border styling.

assertions.description: During async operations (loading configs, creating states/transitions), a loading spinner is displayed in the header area
assertions.expected: A spinning Loader2 icon should appear in the header (ml-auto position) when isLoading is true, indicating an async operation is in progress
preconditions: An async operation is in progress

assertions.description: When a config import fails (invalid JSON or missing states/transitions fields), a red error message appears in the Export/Import tab
assertions.expected: After a failed import, a red error message should appear in the Export/Import tab showing the error reason (e.g., 'Invalid config format: missing states or transitions')
